title: Procter & Gamble is Accelerating Revenue Growth as its Costs are Rising
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc updates Procter & Gamble after earnings, under the theme in his title: revenue growth is accelerating while costs are rising. Revenue growth reached 4%, driven by price increases, with volume contributing 2.4 points despite six years of price rises and a consumer trade-down trend — a performance he credits to excellent management over decades. He points to a near-record operating margin over the trailing twelve months and a step up in return on invested capital to about 17% or more since the post-pandemic reopening, against 10–12% in 2017–19. The stock is up 15.5% plus dividends in 2026, which he calls significant risk-adjusted outperformance for one of the least risky stocks in the market. His updated discounted cash flow values the business at $163 per share against a current $166, so he calls it fairly valued on both his DCF and a forward price-to-earnings view, and well within his margin of safety. His bull case is historic operating leverage: about 3% revenue growth has typically delivered 6% or more EPS growth when costs stay flat, and analysts expect about 5% EPS growth, helped by productivity and selective price rises. The bear case is the bottom line: commodity, energy and freight costs, especially in North America, are rising faster than usual on the Iran war, tariffs and geopolitical shipping costs, in a weak consumer-spending environment. The call is PG — BUY reiterated with high confidence, for a five-to-ten-year hold.
